newsitem.title: USA: Court is asked to undo Centennial deals.
newsitem.headline: Court is asked to undo Centennial deals.

text.p: The former owner of three high-tech start-ups sold to Centennial Technologies Inc in 1996 has filed a lawsuit seeking to undo the $40 million deal, the plaintiff's lawyer said Wednesday.
Centennial shares were trading in the 30s when the stock-swap transaction with Florida businessman Hamby Hutcheson closed last year.
The shares later plummeted amid allegations of fraud at Centennial and the jailing of its former chief executive Emanuel Pinez on charges of insider trading.
"I think it has been made unarguably clear that the (Centennial) financial statements we used were unreliable," said Bruce Bowden, a lawyer for Hutcheson.

The lawsuit, filed in state court and transferred to U.S. District Court in West Palm Beach, Fla., asks that Centennial's purchases of privately held Intelligent Truck Project Inc, Fleet.Net Inc and Smart Traveler Plazas Inc be cancelled.
No court dates have been set, Bowden said.
Hutcheson was reported in talks about a lucrative telecommunications contract worth about $250 million when he sold his companies to Centennial.
The prospect of that contract helped drive up Centennial shares in 1996, when it was the best performing stock on the New York Stock Exchange.
Officials of Centennial were not available for comment on the lawsuit.
